title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey regulators fined DataOne, the operator of a large data center campus in Vineland, $1.07 million for violating the state’s Air Pollution Control Act. During a late July inspection, officials found 62 natural gas generators, each the size of a tractor-trailer and rated at 2,000 kilowatts, running without the required installation or operating permits. The state said this is the largest penalty ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey. The planned complex will cover 2.6 million square feet and require 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium size city, with completion expected by the end of the year.

Governor Mikie Sherrill said such projects must benefit New Jersey communities and cannot be a free ride. Some parts of the complex are already in use, and residents have complained about persistent noise. A group of homeowners has filed a federal lawsuit against DataOne, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued noise violation orders. The article does not say what DataOne’s next steps will be.
